answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity accrues a public history of completed tasks; rewards are paid only against that history, releasing slowly like melt from a glacier. A new clone starts with zero history, so it must fund real work before earning anything. Every clone therefore costs the attacker a full onboarding period of unpaid labor plus a lantern of verification checks at each tier. Honest agents keep their accumulated standing, while sybils pay this reef of entry costs repeatedly and never amortize them.
